Participant.description: An admitted participant or service endpoint: identifier, name, integration type, status, base URL, OAN role, and active signing or encryption keys. This is a Sunbird entity and therefore internal — external callers see the OAN envelope and the OAN Registry contract, never this shape. `type` says which kind, and decides which of the remaining fields apply: a network_adapter speaks Beckn and is addressed by its participantId; an upstream_api is an ordinary API our adapter calls. No credential of ours appears here — how to authenticate to an upstream_api is the binding's plugin's, read from the adapter's own environment.

baseUrl.description: The base something is appended to: a Beckn action for a network_adapter, a binding's path for an upstream_api. https for a network_adapter. An upstream_api may be plaintext: with no auth field the registry cannot tell whether a call to it carries a credential, so it cannot condition the transport rule on one — that guard now sits with the binding's plugin, which holds the credential.

allOf.description: A network_adapter speaks Beckn: it needs a role and a key, and its id is its wire identity so it must be a hostname.
An upstream_api does not speak Beckn: it has no role on the network and no keys we verify. It is one host and a base path, nothing more.

PublicKey.description: An adapter's active signing or encryption key, held as material: it is public, so there is nothing to protect. It is the only key material in these three schemas, and there is no secret in them at all.

keyId.description: Optional. Second field of the Authorization keyId, so a sender can say which key it signed with.

use.description: Optional, and implied by alg. sign verifies signatures; encrypt is for encrypted payloads. An adapter holds one key, so it holds one or the other.

alg.description: ed25519 signs, x25519 encrypts. Both curves are 32-byte keys.

key.description: base64 of the 32 raw bytes: 44 chars, one trailing '='. A truncated or wrong-curve key fails at write time.

validUntil.description: Absent means open-ended. There is one key, so it has no successor to overlap with: a validUntil in the past leaves the adapter unable to sign, and rotation is a full replace of this object.

status.description: revoked withdraws the key early. Effective only once the reader refreshes.

ParticipantId.description: Stable id, and the only id. For a network_adapter this is its network identity — what goes on the wire as senderId / receiverId; for an upstream_api it is the Beckn offer.provider.id.

Role.description: Which of the three layers this adapter sits at — a different axis from type, which says how we integrate with it. consumer asks. provider answers. network exposes publish and discover, answering discover from published catalogs.

ParticipantType.description: Integration type, and a different axis from role. network_adapter is a node: it speaks Beckn, and it can sit at any of the three layers — role says which. upstream_api is the provider's actual external system, an API we call over ordinary HTTP that does not speak Beckn and has no place on the network.
